es: Distinguir obligación, prohibición, permiso y ausencia de obligación en normas escolares y vecinales (must, have to, be required to, must not, be permitted to, don't have to) y reconocer el marcador de cada una.

teaching.en: Under the school regulations, all students are required to wear the uniform and to comply with the dress code in every lesson.
teaching.es: Según el reglamento del colegio, todos los alumnos deben llevar el uniforme y cumplir con el código de vestimenta en todas las clases.
teaching.explanationEs: Be required to + verbo: obligación formal; el reglamento no dice «debes», sino «se exige». Comply with + norma: cumplirla.
segments: Under the school regulations, all students are required to wear the
uniform and to comply with the dress code in every lesson.
teaching.audioText: Under the school regulations, all students are required to wear the uniform and to comply with the dress code in every lesson.

teaching.en: Attendance at the morning assembly is compulsory, whereas joining the choir is entirely optional, so nobody can be forced to sing.
teaching.es: La asistencia a la asamblea de la mañana es obligatoria, mientras que unirse al coro es totalmente opcional, así que nadie puede ser obligado a cantar.
teaching.explanationEs: Compulsory (y mandatory) son adjetivos de obligación propios de los reglamentos; optional marca lo que cada uno decide.
segments: Attendance at the morning assembly is compulsory, whereas joining the choir
is entirely optional, so nobody can be forced to sing.
teaching.audioText: Attendance at the morning assembly is compulsory, whereas joining the choir is entirely optional, so nobody can be forced to sing.

teaching.en: Mobile phones are strictly prohibited during lessons, although students are permitted to use them at break in the yard.
teaching.es: Los teléfonos celulares están estrictamente prohibidos durante las clases, aunque los alumnos tienen permiso para usarlos en el recreo en el patio.
teaching.explanationEs: Are prohibited: prohibición formal, equivale a must not. Are permitted to + verbo: permiso formal, equivale a may o are allowed to.
segments: Mobile phones are strictly prohibited during lessons, although students are
permitted to use them at break in the yard.
teaching.audioText: Mobile phones are strictly prohibited during lessons, although students are permitted to use them at break in the yard.

teaching.en: Sixth-form students will be exempt from the uniform rule, so they don't have to wear it, but wearing it is not forbidden either.
teaching.es: Los alumnos de bachillerato estarán exentos de la norma del uniforme, así que no tienen que llevarlo, pero llevarlo tampoco está prohibido.
teaching.explanationEs: Be exempt from + norma: quedar libre de una obligación. No tener que hacer algo (don't have to) no equivale a tenerlo prohibido (forbidden).
segments: Sixth-form students will be exempt from the uniform rule, so they don't
have to wear it, but wearing it is not forbidden either.
teaching.audioText: Sixth-form students will be exempt from the uniform rule, so they don't have to wear it, but wearing it is not forbidden either.

teaching.en: Staff must not park in front of the gate, because the obligation to keep the entrance clear applies to everyone without exception.
teaching.es: El personal no debe estacionar frente a la puerta, porque la obligación de mantener despejada la entrada se aplica a todos sin excepción.
teaching.explanationEs: Must not = prohibido. Ojo: no equivale a don't have to, que solo dice «no hace falta». Obligation es el sustantivo de lo que se debe hacer.
segments: Staff must not park in front of the gate, because the
obligation to keep the entrance clear applies to everyone without exception.
teaching.audioText: Staff must not park in front of the gate, because the obligation to keep the entrance clear applies to everyone without exception.

teaching.en: Although the final exam is mandatory for everybody, the regulations leave the choice of project topic to each student.
teaching.es: Aunque el examen final es obligatorio para todos, el reglamento deja a cada alumno la elección del tema del proyecto.
teaching.explanationEs: Mandatory = obligatorio, sin excepción. Although + oración: contraste, no lleva but en la misma frase.
segments: Although the final exam is mandatory for everybody, the regulations
leave the choice of project topic to each student.
teaching.audioText: Although the final exam is mandatory for everybody, the regulations leave the choice of project topic to each student.

choices.text: Locking a bicycle at the gate.
Riding a bicycle in the playground.
Cycling to school in the morning.

feedback.es: Are prohibited expresa una prohibición formal; permitted da permiso y optional deja la decisión libre.

origin.text: School notice: bicycles are prohibited in the playground, but pupils are permitted to lock them at the gate. Nobody is forced to cycle to school, because it is optional.

prompt.es: Completa: «La asistencia a la asamblea es obligatoria para todo el colegio.»

feedback.es: Compulsory (o mandatory) califica una obligación que no admite excepción.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo de obligación que aparece en los reglamentos.

origin.text: Every pupil has to be in the hall at nine. Attendance at the assembly is ___ for the whole school, and nobody can be excused without a note.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los visitantes no tienen permiso para entrar en la cocina.»

answer.text: Visitors are not permitted to enter the kitchen

feedback.es: Are not permitted to + verbo base es una prohibición formal; la negación va tras are.

hint.es: Empieza con Visitors; la negación va justo después de are.

prompt.es: Escucha a la directora y elige qué es obligatorio para los alumnos.

choices.text: Wearing a tie to every lesson of the school day.
Keeping their phones switched off for the whole break.
Signing in at the office when they arrive late.

feedback.es: Quien llega tarde debe firmar en la oficina: es obligatorio. La corbata es opcional y los celulares están permitidos en el recreo.

origin.audio: At the start of term, the head teacher read out the regulations. Every student is required to wear the uniform, she said, and arriving on time is compulsory: anyone who comes late must sign in at the office. Mobile phones are prohibited in class, although students are permitted to use them during break. Wearing a tie is optional, so nobody has to buy one, but running in the corridors is forbidden, for safety. She added that staff would comply with the same rules whenever they walked through the school with pupils.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la fuerza de la norma.

pairs: All pupils are required to wear a badge.
Bags are forbidden in the laboratory.
You may leave early on Fridays.
Year eleven will be exempt from assembly.

feedback.es: Required marca obligación, forbidden prohibición, may permiso y be exempt from una liberación de la obligación.

pairs: All pupils are required to wear a badge.
Bags are forbidden in the laboratory.
You may leave early on Fridays.
Year eleven will be exempt from assembly.

prompt.es: Lee el boletín: ¿qué postura refleja sobre la corbata?

choices.text: It accepts a small change while keeping the main rule.
It lowers its standards to cut costs for families.
It tightens the uniform rule after complaints from parents.

feedback.es: La corbata pasa a ser opcional, pero el uniforme sigue siendo obligatorio: un cambio pequeño que mantiene la norma principal.

origin.text: Dear parents, from September the uniform will remain compulsory, but the tie becomes optional. The school believes the change will reduce costs without lowering standards. Staff will check the uniform during the first week, and any student who is not in full uniform will be asked to comply by the next day.

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige qué es obligatorio para los dueños de perros.

choices.text: Walking the dog on the grass near the playground.
Keeping the dog on a lead in the park.
Leaving the dog at home on weekend mornings.

feedback.es: Mandatory marca la obligación: el perro va con correa en el resto del parque. Pasear por la hierba es un permiso.

origin.audio: At the residents' meeting, the meeting leader explained the new street rules. Dogs are forbidden in the playground, he said, but owners are permitted to walk them on the grass. Keeping a dog on a lead is mandatory in the rest of the park, and anyone who fails to comply with that rule may be fined. Cycling on the pavement is prohibited, although children under ten are exempt from it, since they are still learning to ride.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿con qué fin menciona el moderador la multa?

choices.text: To announce a new fine for cyclists on the pavement.
To ask owners to pay for damage.
To show that the lead rule will be taken seriously.

feedback.es: La multa se menciona como consecuencia de no cumplir la norma de la correa: subraya que se aplicará en serio.

origin.audio: At the residents' meeting, the meeting leader explained the new street rules. Dogs are forbidden in the playground, he said, but owners are permitted to walk them on the grass. Keeping a dog on a lead is mandatory in the rest of the park, and anyone who fails to comply with that rule may be fined. Cycling on the pavement is prohibited, although children under ten are exempt from it, since they are still learning to ride.

prompt.es: Completa: «Todo el personal debe cumplir con el nuevo reglamento.»

feedback.es: Comply with + norma significa cumplirla; se construye con with.

origin.text: The new regulations apply from Monday. All staff are required to ___ with them, or they may be fined.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es obligatorio llevar el uniforme en todas las clases.»

answer.text: Wearing the uniform is mandatory in every lesson

feedback.es: Mandatory es el adjetivo de obligación sin excepción; wearing el uniforme funciona como sujeto de la frase.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué quiere dejar claro la profesora sobre la norma de la piscina?

choices.text: That the rule protects young children rather than spoiling fun.
That older pupils may swim alone whenever they like.
That children under ten may swim only during lessons.

feedback.es: Dice que el objetivo no es estropear la diversión sino proteger a los más pequeños: la norma protege y no limita por limitar.

origin.audio: A sign at the pool says that children under ten may not swim without an adult, and a teacher explained the rule to a group of pupils. The aim is not to spoil anyone's fun, she said, but to keep the younger children safe. Older pupils are permitted to swim alone, provided that a lifeguard is here, and nobody is required to join the lesson if they have a note from home.

prompt.es: Lee el aviso: ¿qué se puede deducir?

choices.text: A jacket is compulsory, but the logo is left to each person.
A jacket is optional, but any jacket that staff wear must carry the logo.
A jacket is optional, and so is the logo on it.

feedback.es: El aviso no obliga a llevar chaqueta, pero impone una condición a quien la lleve: el logotipo.

origin.text: Notice to staff: wearing a name badge is required in all public areas. Staff are not forced to wear a jacket, but the regulations are clear that any jacket that staff wear at work must carry the company logo.

prompt.es: Completa: «Traer tu propio almuerzo es opcional, así que no tienes que traerlo.»

feedback.es: Optional describe lo que cada uno decide; don't have to confirma que traer el almuerzo no es obligatorio.

origin.text: The canteen is open every day. Bringing your own lunch is ___, so you don't have to bring one.
